name: Caveman
works_with: Skill: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Copilot and 30+ more. Proxy: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Aider, Kilo, Qwen, OpenCode, Hermes, OpenClaw and Pi
short: Cuts tokens two ways: a skill that makes your agent answer in short plain sentences, and a proxy that shrinks what it reads.
what: Caveman has two parts. The skill changes how your agent replies: answer first, short sentences, with code, commands, paths and numbers kept exact. The CLI proxy compresses logs, CSV, YAML, JSON and test output before the agent reads them. In the project's own benchmark that meant 33.2% fewer input tokens across whole Claude Code sessions, with 18 of 18 answers right.
who: Anyone paying per token or running into context limits with a coding agent. If you pay per request instead (GitHub Copilot premium requests, for example), the README says shorter answers cost the same, so skip it.
needs: For the skill: a coding agent that supports skills
For the proxy: Node.js 22.13 or later, plus your own model keys or Claude Pro/Max login

steps.title: Just the skill, for shorter answers
Or the Claude Code plugin
steps.text: It starts on its own in every interactive session, subagents included.
steps.code: claude plugin marketplace add JuliusBrussee/caveman && claude plugin install caveman@caveman

steps.title: The proxy, to shrink what the agent reads
steps.text: After the first run, plain `claude` keeps using it.
steps.code:
npm install -g @caveman-ai/cli && caveman setup --install
caveman claude        # or codex · gemini · aider · kilo · qwen · opencode · hermes · openclaw · pi

steps.title: See where your tokens go
steps.code:
caveman learn                 # rank where your tokens go, from agent history already on disk
caveman stats                 # your token history

steps.title: Uninstall
steps.text: On npm 12 or newer, add `--allow-git=root` too.

try.label: From the README
try.text:
/caveman

Also try /ultracave for even shorter replies and /caveman-review for one-line review findings. Say "stop caveman" to go back. In Codex, type $caveman.

watch: The caveman CLI sends usage stats by default: commands run, token counts, a random install ID, OS and IP. It doesn't send prompts, code or file paths. Turn it off with `caveman telemetry off` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`.
The skill on its own runs on your machine and sends nothing.
The proxy runs with your keys and your Claude Pro/Max login.
The install-everywhere option pipes a script from the internet into bash. Read the script before you run it.
HTML has no compressor yet. In the benchmark, the HTML session came out 9.9% worse.
